headline: Crude bombs and arson: Buses torched and blasts rock Dhaka
summary: Multiple crude bombs exploded across the city, including inside Dhaka University and the CID headquarters, while three buses were set on fire.
details: Criminals exploded crude bombs in several areas of Dhaka, including inside Dhaka University and the CID headquarters, and torched three buses in Bhatara, Dhamrai, and Savar.
At Dhaka University, a series of explosions rocked at least six different parts of the campus, including the TSC area, Senate Building, and Nilkhet intersection.
Students caught three suspects—Rezaul Karim, 42, of Natore; Sohel Rana, 33, of Rajshahi; and Nazmus Saad, 33, of Gopalganj—in the TSC area and handed them over to police.
A crude bomb was hurled into the CID headquarters compound in Malibagh from the Moghbazar-Mouchak Flyover, exploding near a Special Branch vehicle.
Another blast occurred in front of Sony Cinema Hall in Mirpur-1, while a school bus in Bhatara was set ablaze on 100 Feet Road.
In Savar and Dhamrai, two public transport buses were torched in the early morning hours, with police suspecting political activists behind the attacks.
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) stated that these incidents are aimed at creating panic among the public and suspect a particular group is deliberately carrying out sabotage.
Police have strengthened intelligence-led operations, increased deployment and introduced mobile patrols to ensure public safety while analyzing CCTV footage to identify suspects.
caption:
Buses torched and crude bombs exploded across Dhaka in a series of coordinated attacks aimed at creating public panic.

Criminals exploded crude bombs in several areas of Dhaka, including inside Dhaka University and the CID headquarters, and torched three buses in Bhatara, Dhamrai, and Savar.

At Dhaka University, a series of explosions rocked at least six different parts of the campus, including the TSC area, Senate Building, and Nilkhet intersection.

Students caught three suspects—Rezaul Karim, 42, of Natore; Sohel Rana, 33, of Rajshahi; and Nazmus Saad, 33, of Gopalganj—in the TSC area and handed them over to police.

A crude bomb was hurled into the CID headquarters compound in Malibagh from the Moghbazar-Mouchak Flyover, exploding near a Special Branch vehicle.

Another blast occurred in front of Sony Cinema Hall in Mirpur-1, while a school bus in Bhatara was set ablaze on 100 Feet Road.

In Savar and Dhamrai, two public transport buses were torched in the early morning hours, with police suspecting political activists behind the attacks.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) stated that these incidents are aimed at creating panic among the public and suspect a particular group is deliberately carrying out sabotage.

Police have strengthened intelligence-led operations, increased deployment and introduced mobile patrols to ensure public safety while analyzing CCTV footage to identify suspects.

headline_marked: Tongi drug gang [[held DT journalists hostage and tortured them]] at gunpoint
headline: Tongi drug gang held DT journalists hostage and tortured them at gunpoint
summary: Journalists from the Dhaka Tribune were targeted and assaulted by a drug syndicate in Tongi, highlighting the dangers of reporting on crime empires.
details: Journalists from the Dhaka Tribune were held hostage and tortured at gunpoint by a drug gang operating in Tongi.
The incident occurred while the reporters were investigating the area's drug trade, exposing the violent methods used by these syndicates to silence journalists.
The attack underscores the risks associated with reporting on the narcotics trade in the region.
Tongi is known for having a drug empire where gangs continue to defy repeated law enforcement crackdowns.
The victims suffered injuries as a result of the torture, as seen in the evidence of their physical trauma.
The Dhaka Tribune continues to report on the evidence of the drug gang's influence and the law enforcement's struggle to maintain control in the area.
